Seoul in Winter 2026: What to Do, Where to Go & How to Stay Warm

A complete guide to visiting Seoul in winter — best activities, festivals, ski resorts, what to wear, and why winter might be the best time to visit.

⏱ 8 min read · 🇰🇷 Seoul, Korea · Updated 2026

Seoul in Winter — Cold, Clear, and Surprisingly Wonderful

Seoul winters are cold — genuinely cold. December through February brings temperatures that regularly drop below -10°C, with biting winds that make it feel colder. But this is not a reason to avoid Seoul in winter. It's a reason to embrace it. The city is breathtaking under snow, the air is crystal clear, the crowds are dramatically thinner than spring and autumn, and you'll have attractions practically to yourself. Plus, Korean winter food is extraordinary.

🌡️ What to Expect Temperature-Wise

  • December: -2°C to 5°C. First snows possible from mid-December.
  • January: Coldest month. -8°C to 2°C average. Can hit -15°C with wind chill.
  • February: Still cold but slowly warming. -5°C to 4°C. Spring hints arrive late February.

Humidity is very low in winter — the cold is dry. This means clear skies, good air quality, and no rain. But your skin will get dry; bring moisturizer.

💡 What to wear: Layer seriously. A good thermal base layer + mid layer + heavy outer coat + gloves + hat is essential. Korean fashion stores (Zara, H&M, Korean brands like Ader Error) sell excellent coats at reasonable prices — you can buy winter gear after you arrive if your luggage is light.

🎿 Ski Resorts Near Seoul

One of winter Seoul's underrated pleasures: world-class ski resorts within 1–2 hours. Most tourists don't know how good Korean skiing is.

Vivaldi Park (비발디파크)

90 minutes from Seoul by shuttle. 21 slopes ranging from beginner to expert. Full-day lift pass around ₩80,000–₩120,000. Equipment rental on-site. One of the most popular with Seoul day-trippers.

Yongpyong Resort (용평리조트)

Host venue for the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics. 28 slopes, Korea's most prestigious ski resort. About 2.5 hours from Seoul. A full winter resort experience with excellent facilities.

Bears Town (베어스타운)

Closest ski resort to Seoul — about 50 minutes. Good for beginners and families. Popular for night skiing (slopes lit until 2am).

💡 Ski trip tip: Book a shuttle package from Seoul that includes transport, lift pass, and equipment rental. Much cheaper than arranging everything separately. Available on Klook and Viator.

🎄 Winter Festivals & Events

Christmas in Seoul

Seoul goes big for Christmas. The Myeongdong area transforms with elaborate light installations. Cheonggyecheon Stream becomes a lantern festival. Lotte World and Everland theme parks have massive Christmas events. The city feels genuinely festive without feeling commercial.

Hwacheon Sancheoneo Ice Festival

About 2 hours northeast of Seoul. Ice fishing, ice sculpture, sledding on a frozen river. Held January–February. One of Korea's most beloved winter festivals and genuinely unique.

Seoul Lantern Festival

Usually held late November–December along Cheonggyecheon Stream. Thousands of illuminated lanterns line the stream creating a magical spectacle. Free to walk through.

🍲 What to Eat in Winter Seoul

Korean winter food is some of the best food you'll ever eat:

  • Hotpot & Shabu-shabu: Perfect for freezing nights. Dip thin-sliced meat and vegetables in bubbling broth. Many restaurants offer unlimited refills.
  • Budae Jjigae (부대찌개): "Army stew" — a hearty mix of spam, hot dogs, ramen, kimchi, and gochujang in a bubbling pot. Warming and delicious.
  • Hotteok (호떡): Street pancakes filled with brown sugar and nuts. Best eaten immediately from the street vendor.
  • Bungeo-ppang (붕어빵): Fish-shaped waffle filled with sweet red bean paste. Sold at street stalls and subway exits in winter only.
  • Makgeolli + Pajeon: Drinking rice wine while eating green onion pancakes during rain or snow is a classic Korean winter tradition.

🏛️ Best Winter Activities in Seoul

  • Palace visits: Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung covered in snow are breathtaking — and have the shortest queues of any season.
  • Jimjilbang (찜질방): Korean bathhouse/sauna. The perfect antidote to a freezing day. ₩10,000–₩15,000 for unlimited time. Many open 24 hours.
  • Indoor markets: Gwangjang and Namdaemun markets are fully covered and warm — great winter alternatives to outdoor exploration.
  • Cafe hopping: Seoul's cafe scene really shines in winter. Warm, beautifully designed spaces for hours of relaxation.
  • Coex Mall: The massive underground mall in Gangnam. Includes the Instagram-famous Starfield Library. Could spend a full day here.

💰 Winter Travel Budget Benefits

Winter is genuinely the best time to visit Seoul on a budget:

  • Hotel prices 20–40% lower than spring and autumn peak seasons
  • No need to book months in advance
  • Fewer crowds at popular attractions
  • Shorter queues everywhere
  • Some restaurants offer winter specials and promotions
